scope: Proposition 7.3 (Directional bootstrap) of the manuscript “Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions” (preprints/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 078 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ea18d159eefcdc7f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 57. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 0 < s ≤ 1. Let a sequence of pair laws of bounded planar parameters (A, B) be dominated, with subpower loss at precision ρ, by the product of two populations having conditional child bounds of rate s. Assume that for each fixed t > 0, both comparison marginals satisfy sup ℓ µ{dist(·, ℓ) ≤ ρt } ≤ ρκt+o(1) for some κt > 0, (7.22) and likewise for the other marginal. Suppose the direction-prefix probabilities conditional on either pin are homogenized on the same pair law. For each finite test, assume a common event of subpower pair mass on which the required original direction bins are uniform and the pair support lies over the simultaneous tested good-parent fibers for the child bounds. Then, on uniform trims, the direction of B − A conditional on either pin has prefix ball dimension at least s. The assertion is hereditary under subpower restrictions which retain the stated child bounds and product comparisons.
